subject: Follow-up: Demo + proposed A/B throughput/latency test window
messages:
From: Peter Nguyen <peter@nimbus.ai>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-04-20T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Thanks — demo recap and quick ask

Laura — thanks for the live demo today. Helpful to see the routing/fallback behavior and the console traces. Two quick follow-ups from our end: 1) we want an apples-to-apples run against the Hyperscaler-managed endpoint (same open model weights, same tokenization and prompts) to validate latency and throughput at scale; and 2) we need a crisp list of what Redwood would run in a production A/B (metrics, sample sizes, and expected artifacts).

High level constraints: we will run the customer traffic simulation next Thurs (4/22) in the US-west region and want the Redwood vs Hyperscaler runs to happen in the same 2-hour window. Can Redwood confirm a proposed test plan and the specific metrics you will surface (p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, QPS, error rates)? Also, how will you account for batching/KV caching differences?

Thanks — Peter
Peter Nguyen
Head of Platform Engineering, Nimbus Corp
From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
To: Peter Nguyen <peter@nimbus.ai>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-04-20T18:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Thanks — demo recap and quick ask

Peter — great to hear, and appreciate the constraints. Short answer: yes, we can run an apples-to-apples A/B window. I outlined a concise test plan below and attached a spreadsheet with the configs. Key points:

- Test models: same open weights (you confirmed v1.3-fp16). We will pin identical model files on both sides.
- Prompts: we will use your sample-prompts.txt (attached) — 3 families: short Q/A, multi-turn support, and long-context summarization (1–2k tokens).
- Load profile: 1k warmup requests then steady-state 6k requests per hour (burst up to 9k/hr) — matches your expected simulation.
- Metrics captured: p50/p90/p95/p99 latency (server-side), tokens/sec (decoded), QPS, tails by request size bucket, error rate, and kernel-level GPU utilization.
- Batching/KV cache: we will run two variants — (A) production-like continuous batching with prefix KV caching enabled, (B) strictly single-request mode (no batching, no cache) to isolate runtime differences. That gives you both realistic and conservative comparisons.
- Sample sizes: we recommend 10k total requests per variant per platform to stabilize p99 estimates; spreadsheet shows how that maps to time windows.

Next steps I propose:
1) Redwood runs variant A and B in the 2-hour window on 4/22 US-west — we will stream logs and post-processed CSVs to the S3 link.
2) Hyperscaler runs the identical workload and provides their raw latencies in the same schema.
3) We produce an A/B summary with p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, and a short slide deck with diffs and artifacts.

Ben and Rishi — can you confirm capacity and the exact invocation command lines so Peter can hand these to Hyperscaler ops? I attached the initial config and prompt set.

Laura Bennett
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-04-21T09:07:00-07:00
Subject: Re: proposed test plan + infra notes

Looping in infra details. We can support the run on our Dedicated fleet in us-west-2 during the 4/22 window. Quick notes:

- Capacity: reserve three GPU workers (A100x2-like) for the 2-hour windows to avoid noisy neighbors.
- Invocation: we will use the same container image and the following invocation for continuous-batch mode:
  - ./redwood-run --model /models/v1.3-fp16 --batching continuous --kv-cache enabled --seq-length 2048 --concurrency 64 --sample-seed 42 --trace-output s3://redwood-shared/nimbus/continuous/
  - For single-request mode: ./redwood-run --batching single --kv-cache disabled --concurrency 1 --trace-output s3://redwood-shared/nimbus/single/
- Measurement hooks: timestamps at recv/start/generation-end/token-close; per-request token counts; GPU util reported every 30s. We will publish a CSV with columns: request_id,start_ms,server_start_ms,gen_end_ms,token_count,error_flag,gpu_util_pct.

On expected magnitude: our internal micro-runs show for this model at 1k concurrent steady state: p95 ~ 160–220 ms (continuous batching, short prompts), p99 ~ 520–700 ms depending on prompt length. Tokens/sec (decoded) on the reserved workers was ~18k tokens/sec for short prompts in our lab. Hyperscaler numbers were higher tail in a couple of public tests we've seen, but we will only compare once both raw traces arrive.

Rishi — can you confirm the exact S3 path and that the CSV schema in the spreadsheet matches our exporter? If yes, I will lock capacity and finalize the command lines.

Ben Carter
Senior Systems Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-04-21T11:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: proposed test plan + infra notes

Confirmed S3 paths and CSV schema. I made two small changes to the spreadsheet: added a request-size bucket column (<=128 tokens, 129-512, 513-2048) and a de-duplicated tokenization hash so we can align token counts across vendors. Link: s3://redwood-shared/nimbus/ab-test-configs.zip (contains exporter, schema, and sample scripts).

I've also scheduled a 30-minute runbook sync at 10:30 PT on 4/22 to validate the live instrumentation and to make sure both sides use the same time source (we'll use NTP and include a time-offset file).

Rishi Malhotra
Principal Performance Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
To: Peter Nguyen <peter@nimbus.ai>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-04-22T09:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Thanks — demo recap and quick ask (Confirmed run details)

Peter — confirming the test window and next steps:

- Redwood will run both variants (continuous-batch + single-request) between 10:00–12:00 PT on 4/22 in us-west-2.
- Attachments: redwood-ab-test-plan.xlsx (config + mapping), sample-prompts.txt, raw-latency-snapshots.csv (example output).
- Deliverables after window: consolidated CSVs (both platforms), a short A/B slide deck with p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec by prompt bucket, and recommendations for any runtime config changes.

As an example of what you'll get in the slide deck: we will show side-by-side p95 numbers for short prompts (expected ~180ms Redwood vs vendor), tokens/sec graphs over the interval, and a tail-latency waterfall that highlights batched vs single-request behavior. If you want us to include kernel-level flame graphs, say the word — Rishi can capture those during the run.

Final ask: please confirm who on your ops side will run the Hyperscaler-side invocation and share the contact so we can include them in the 10:30 PT runbook sync.

Thanks — looking forward to the run.

Laura Bennett
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
